eligibility_rationale: Floral display and reproductive-effort variables are linked to hummingbird pollination, nectar robbing and reproduction across edge-gap contexts; individual trait axes must be separated.
Calyx length and other display traits have pollinator- and seed-predator-mediated selection on relative seed set; each trait must be separated before outcome coding.
Floral pigmentation and correlated morphology are linked to pollinator and seed-predator selection in two populations on fecundity; axes require separation.
Flowering stalk height is one declared coordinate with pollination and seed-predation components linked to seed maturation across populations.
Flowering display is evaluated against hummingbird visitation, nectar robbery and reproductive consequences across disturbance patch types.
Greya visitors include pollinating floral parasites; pollination benefit and seed-parasitism cost are coupled in the same interaction architecture rather than fixed opposing agents.
A floral odor blend is linked to pollinator preference, seed predation and a common reproductive endpoint across an elevational/species panel.
Ant density is ecological context rather than a measured response to the focal floral symmetry/display coordinate, so two function-linked responses on A are not identified.

Fragrance attracts weaver ants that disrupt pollinator visits; the current design identifies an indirect antagonist-mediated pollination cost, not two focal functions independently responding to the fragrance axis.
Flowering schedule and display differences between congeners are linked to pollination, flower/seed predation and fruit production; phenology/display axes require separation.
Flower height is linked to nectar-robbing access, pollinator behavior, pollination success and fruit/seed outcomes; trait variation is observational but the same coordinate is shared.
Flowering stem height is one display axis with pollination success, pollen limitation, seed predation and female reproductive success measured on the same population.
Floral display size is jointly linked to visitor rate/pollination, seed-predator damage and seed set along a spatial elevation/invasion gradient.
Corolla width, herkogamy, display and mating-system traits are linked to pollination and floral parasitism across populations; trait axes must be separated.
Flower size and flower number have pollinator-, nectar-robber- and florivore-linked selection with common reproductive output; axes require separation.
Spotted versus spotless floral morph is one declared coordinate with pollinator preference, florivore ovule predation and reproductive fitness across site contexts.
Corolla tube length and nectar reward are linked to legitimate visitation, nectar robbing and seed production; separate axes are required.
Corolla morphology, nectar gland size and nectar reward predict legitimate pollination, robbery and female fitness across three populations; axes require separation.
Corolla tube and reward traits are linked to pollinator assemblage, nectar robbing and fruit/seed reproduction; separate axes must be frozen.
Individual- and plot-level floral chemodiversity is linked to pollinator and florivore visitor groups plus plant fitness; scale-specific trait axes require separation.
Flower number and display centrality are linked to hummingbird pollinators, nectar robbers/florivores and viable seed production; cluster dependence with SCHPRISMA-000312 must be retained.
Robbery-damaged versus undamaged flower state is generated by the exploiter itself; nectar robbing is the antecedent cause of A rather than an independent response to the resulting A.
Floral exsertion and lower-lip size have pollen-load/pollination and seed-predation components tied to final seed production across fourteen populations.
The common-garden contrast contains a bundle of attractive and defensive traits with pollinator and robbery regimes; no single shared coordinate is yet isolated.
Morphology, reward and resistance-associated traits are correlated with legitimate visitors, nectar robbing and reproductive components, but one shared axis is not yet identified.
Factorial herbivore suppression and pollination treatments estimate selection on multiple reproductive/floral traits on reproductive fitness; trait axes require separation.
Experimental evolution changes defence and floral-trait plasticity under herbivory/pollination regimes, but no single shared trait coordinate is identified.
